properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 27 at 4:11PM PST until November 28 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 6.8 feet
will peak near Noon Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 4:11PM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2
feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 27 at 4:06PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Some
locations will experience zero visibility for several hours. This
dense fog event will be a Level 4 on a scale of 1 to 5.

* WHERE...Much of central California.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to Noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dense fog will make driving conditions hazardous leading
to a high transportation risk.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dense fog will resemble that of the past two
days. Low clouds will quickly become dense fog shortly after
sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this
evening, if you are traveling.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your low beam headlights, and leave plenty
of distance ahead of you. Consider leaving after the dense fog has
gone. Be sure to change your headlights from AUTO to MANUAL, since
automatic headlights will not activate in the dense fog.

properties.areaDesc: Pasquotank; Camden; Western Currituck; Eastern Currituck; Virginia Beach
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 7:00PM EST until November 27 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1 foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Pasquotank, Camden, Western
Currituck and Eastern Currituck Counties. In Virginia,
Virginia Beach.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM EST THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Dorchester; Wicomico; Somerset
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 27 at 7:00PM EST until November 27 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Two to three feet of inundation above ground level in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Dorchester, Wicomico and Somerset Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate to locally major flooding may cause
extensive inundation and flooding of numerous roads and
buildings resulting in a significant threat to property and
life. Water will be 2 to 3 feet or more above ground level in
some areas. Flooding may extend inland from the waterfront and
shoreline flooding homes, businesses and isolating some
neighborhoods. Numerous roads may become impassable under
several feet of water and cars submerged.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.

deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 27 at 6:59PM AST until November 29 at 8:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Northern to eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:19PM PST until November 27 at 5:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides,
will bring around 2.2 to 2.6 ft of inundation above ground
level in low-lying areas and shore lines during high tide
Friday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the
communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold
Beach, and Coos Bay. Also, portions of Highway 101, especially
around Coos Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST today. High tide today occurred at 12:44
PM at Port Orford and 1:14 PM at Charleston. The risk of
inundation continues a couple hours after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying lots, parks, and roads with
some road closures expected, especially along immediate
coastlines, tidal estuaries, and sloughs. Some shoreline
erosion will occur.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 27 at 1:14PM PST until November 28 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM PST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage early tomorrow
afternoon to 16.3 feet late tomorrow evening.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.1
feet on 12/15/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM PST.

abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.

local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri
11/27, +1.7 ft MHHW (6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28, +1.2
ft MHHW (6.1 ft MLLW) at 4:53 PM Sun 11/29, and +0.7 ft MHHW
(5.6 ft MLLW) at 7:25 AM Mon 11/30.
* West Sacramento: +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri
11/27, +1.8 ft MHHW (6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28, +1.4
ft MHHW (5.8 ft MLLW) at 8:03 PM Sun 11/29, and +1.0 ft MHHW
(5.4 ft MLLW) at 9:18 PM Mon 11/30.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+7.4 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28, +7.1 ft at 7:00 PM Sun 11/29,
+6.8 ft at 9:00 AM Mon 11/30, and +5.9 ft at 10:00 PM Tue
12/01.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 3:32AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:

this morning but do shift to the west in the afternoon with peak
gusts upwards of 40 mph. The combination of snow and wind will
result in reduced visibility below 1 mile at times, especially
between 3PM and 10PM. Expect additional snow accumulations between 1
and 3 inches.

The steadiest snow and strongest wind will end by midnight with
improving conditions thereafter.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
